requirements.requirement: On node1, run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: A root-owned cron definition contains the exact daily 02:15 schedule. The target script is valid and executable, and crond was enabled and active both before and after restart. The node uses America/New_York local time.

The cron command appends both stdout and stderr to the requested path. Direct tests produced timestamped output, increased the log from one to two lines, and showed that existing output and configuration persisted across restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The exact daily cron schedule is active and persistent, and append-based logging works and survives restart. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and disruption, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered system, crond, configuration, retained data, and command behavior.
limitations: No scheduler-originated firing at exactly 02:15 was captured; daily recurrence is inferred from the directly observed cron entry and active crond service, while the configured command and append behavior were tested manually.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Repairing the malformed, non-executable prepared script was necessary to run the requested command (cmd-aac9381cbdd04e6b); creating the secured log and cron definition directly implemented the task (cmd-2159302ee5914623, cmd-a064a723b9474004); the two manual appends were bounded functional evidence and retained only legitimate command output (cmd-3aa45645065d42fd, cmd-13b1e5eed7614231); and the transient reboot action fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-28ee3f06fd0b4645). Afterward, SELinux remained enforcing with appropriate labels, no services were failed, package health remained clean, and listening sockets showed only reboot-related PID changes.
